objective: Decide, within 48 hours, whether a daily residual-reversal book (industry and PCA residuals, three liquid universes, 5 and 21 day lookbacks, 1 and 5 day holds, 100 names per side, turnover/news/VIX conditions and ridge/LightGBM rankers as second-stage robustness) keeps a net Sharpe after measured costs in the 2024-2026 window and is uncorrelated enough with the existing stock long-short book to be a paper sub-strategy of the quant1 account.
target_regime_and_horizon: US stocks and ETF hedge, top 500/1000/3000 by ADV, signals at the close of t from 5 or 21 sessions of residual returns, 1 or 5 session holds as overlapping batches, trade at the open of t+1 (close of t+1 as a robustness cell). Judged on 2024-01-08..2026-09-15 and by market phase; 2017-10..2023-08 only for crash veto and diagnostics; the regime in which it should work is high cross-sectional dispersion / elevated VIX (Nagel 2012), the failure signal is a negative 63-session z of the book and breakdown of the PCA residual explanatory share.
existing_solution_comparison: Published residual-reversal stat-arb: Avellaneda-Lee PCA 1.44 net (1997-2007, 0.9 in 2003-07, 5 bp, cap above 1 bn), Blitz et al. monthly residual reversal net of costs among large caps after 1990, Da-Liu-Schaumburg monthly Sharpe 0.52 vs 0.14, DLSA about 1.5 on 550 stocks with a learned model (2002-2016), Attention Factors 2.3 net with costs in the objective (to 2021). Independent post-2019 evidence is negative: the equity-statarb repo (CRSP, daily sector residual) has OOS 2019-2024 gross 0.23, net -0.15 at 7 bp. Funds run this class at scale with execution infrastructure; our edge, if any, is the measured liquid-name spread model and a short-capable book at small size.
remaining_evidence_gap: No published or open number for a daily residual-reversal book in 2024-2026 with measured spread/impact/borrow, a PCA residual versus beta/industry residual comparison on the same data, or the VIX/turnover/news conditions out of sample. Our own panel can supply exactly that.
negative_experiments_checked: Registry rows read (last row each): sector_residual_reversal_statarb_decay (external negative, reopened because shorts are in scope and costs are measured), news_vs_nonews_drop_reversal (refuted: event study of >=5% drops in ADV top 1500, 12 candidates, best Sharpe 0.67; this book is a cross-sectional rank book, different estimator, the news condition is one cell group and the overlap is disclosed), no_news_price_shock_reversal_chan (harvested, monthly), etf_constituent_lead_lag_reversion and letf_close_rebalancing_flow_reversal (ETF-level, refuted, not reopened), deep_learning_stat_arb_residual (not executable then; this is its engine), end_of_day_reversal (parked, minute data, not touched), cross_sectional_gap_fade (closed one-day round trips, not touched); t20261005_p1_s0_decay (P1 Stage 0 measurement of REV5/RREV5 decay, overlapping objects, disclosed in contract.md section 0).
cost_and_execution_assumptions: Decision at the close of t; trade at the open of t+1 (close of t+1 robustness only) through backtest.run_book; costfn.make_cost_fn (cost_model_v1 half spread by price/ADV/vol/year plus square-root impact at actual dollars of a 300,000 USD sub-account, 0.5 bp fees); borrow 25 bp a year (100 bp stress) on shorts in the easy-to-borrow proxy only; 0.5x/1x/2x cost scaling; ADV participation reported and flagged above 1%.
stop_condition: Stage A (24 main cells, recent window) is the decisive cheap test: if no cell has gross Sharpe above 0.3 the family is closed at this depth; a negative verdict needs all five depth conditions (reproduction, faithful implementation, three-point scale curves, full preregistered budget, adequate power), otherwise the verdict is 'not at depth' with the missing item. Compute stop: 48 hours from 2026-10-06 22:41 UTC, Modal cap 4 USD.

cheapest_decisive_test.action: Stage A: full run_book engine over 2024-01-08..2026-09-15 for the 24 main cells (4 robustness and 2 model cells follow on the selected spec), gross, cost components and net per cell; first batch L=5, H=5, three universes, industry and PCA residuals within 24 hours.
cheapest_decisive_test.pass_condition: At least one cell reaches recent net Sharpe above 0 at 1x cost and the 2x-cost net is above half of it; then Stage B scoring with scorecard_v2 (DSR >= 0.70 with N = 24, net placebo >= 0.90, robustness >= 3, no veto) for P1.
cheapest_decisive_test.falsification_condition: Every cell has recent gross Sharpe < 0.3 or net Sharpe <= 0 at 1x cost with consistent sign across universes and executions, and the five depth conditions are met: then the family is not viable at this depth.

sources.claim: Guijarro-Ordonez, Pelger and Zanotti (Deep Learning Statistical Arbitrage, arXiv 2106.04028): on about 550 liquid US stocks, out of sample 2002-2016, the Sharpe ratio of the learned residual stat-arb policy has a half-life of about seven trading days over the holding period, is still above one at a 22-day holding period with a 1-day objective, and reaches about 1.5 when the multi-day holding period is optimized directly (Figure 12).
sources.core_claim: The half-life in terms of Sharpe ratios is around seven trading days. In fact, the Sharpe ratio is still above one with a one month (22 business days) holding period
sources.applicability: Sets the trading-speed grid (kappa 1..0.05, full rebalance every 5 or 21 sessions) and the lag range 1..22 of the decay curve; Stage 1 of P1 replicates this model.
sources.independent_replication: One independent partial replication (bsiranosian blog); the only 2016-2024 replication (arXiv 2412.11432) was withdrawn.
sources.limitations: Authors' backtest, ends 2016, 5 bp per transaction plus 1 bp short fee; learned signal, not the linear library signals measured here.
sources.market_and_period: about 550 liquid US stocks, out of sample 2002-2016, daily

sources.claim: Da, Liu and Schaumburg (NY Fed Staff Report 513; Management Science 2014): the standard short-term reversal profit decomposes into across-industry momentum, within-industry expected-return variation, under-reaction to within-industry cash-flow news and a residual; only the residual is significant and positive, and a strategy built to capture it earns a risk-adjusted return three times the standard reversal over 1982-2009.
sources.core_claim: A simple short-term return reversal trading strategy designed to capture the residual component generates a highly significant risk-adjusted return three times the size of the standard reversal strategy during our 1982-2009 sampling period.
sources.applicability: Motivates IREV5 (within-industry reversal) and RREV5/RREV21 (risk-model residual reversal) next to raw REV5.
sources.independent_replication: Blitz, Huij, Lansdorp and Verbeek (2013) report a similar gain for residual reversal on another construction (practitioner summary only, not read in full).
sources.limitations: Monthly reversal, 1982-2009, gross of costs; our test is daily on 2017-2026 U3000 with measured close costs.

sources.claim: Lou, Polk and Skouras (A Tug of War: Overnight Versus Intraday Expected Returns, JFE 2019): momentum profits accrue overnight and partly reverse intraday, while other anomaly returns accrue intraday, so overnight and intraday components of past returns carry different information.
sources.core_claim: A Tug of War: Overnight Versus Intraday
sources.applicability: Motivates ON5 and ID5 as separate inputs; the paper gives no clear sign for a 5-day component predicting total close-to-close returns, so their signs are fixed on the stress window before the recent window judges them.
sources.independent_replication: Related: Akbas et al. 2022, Hendershott-Livdan-Rosch 2020 (not read here).
sources.limitations: Monthly portfolios, 1993-2013; our components are 5-day means on 2017-2026.

sources.claim: Avellaneda and Lee (Statistical Arbitrage in the US Equities Market, Quantitative Finance 2010): residuals of stock returns on PCA or sector-ETF factors are traded as mean-reverting processes; after transaction costs PCA-based strategies have an average annual Sharpe ratio of 1.44 over 1997-2007 but only 0.9 over 2003-2007, and ETF-based strategies 1.1 with a similar degradation after 2002.
sources.core_claim: during 2003-2007, the average Sharpe ratio of PCA-based strategies was only 0.9
sources.applicability: RREV5/RREV21 use the project's risk-model residuals (industry + style factors) as the residual definition; the OU-threshold rule itself is a Stage 1 baseline, not measured here.
sources.independent_replication: Widely replicated; recent net performance poor in Attention Factors' comparison.
sources.limitations: 1997-2007; thresholds and costs differ from ours.

sources.claim: Attention Factors for statistical arbitrage (arXiv 2510.11616): with 5 bp per transaction, the parametric (OU-style) residual model falls to negative net Sharpe because of turnover, a simple PCA factor model reaches about 1.5 net, and the end-to-end model with costs in the objective reaches about 2.3 net (authors' backtest, 500 US stocks to 2021).
sources.core_claim: unprecedented performance of 2.3 after trading costs
sources.applicability: Shallow single-signal or threshold rules fail on costs; Stage 0 therefore measures speed curves and composites, and P1 Stage 1 puts costs into the objective.
sources.limitations: Authors' own backtest ending 2021; flat 5 bp costs.

sources.claim: Frazzini, Israel and Moskowitz (Trading Costs of Asset Pricing Anomalies, NBER draft 2012, AQR live executions): size, value and momentum survive costs at fund sizes of tens of billions, while short-term reversal does not survive at sizes above about $9 billion in the US.
sources.core_claim: Short-term reversal strategies, on the other hand, do not survive transactions costs at sizes greater than $9 billion in the U.S.
sources.applicability: Reversal is cost-constrained at institutional size but our book is small (E = $1M for impact), so the binding cost is the spread; Stage 0 uses the measured close half-spread by stock and year.
sources.independent_replication: Consistent with Novy-Marx-Velikov; final published version not read.
sources.limitations: Institutional execution 1998-2011; capacity, not small-account economics.

sources.claim: Blitz, Huij, Lansdorp and Verbeek (Short-term residual reversal, Journal of Financial Markets 16(3) 2013, 477-504; abstract from the Erasmus repository record): a reversal strategy on Fama-French residual returns avoids the dynamic factor exposures of conventional reversal and earns twice its risk-adjusted return; it is significant net of trading costs even for large caps after 1990.
sources.core_claim: Residual reversal strategies generate statistically and economically significant profits net of trading costs, even when we restrict our sample to large-cap stocks over the post-1990 period.
sources.applicability: Second independent source for RREV5/RREV21; supports measuring residual reversal on the liquid L12 bucket with net costs.
sources.independent_replication: Da-Liu-Schaumburg reach the same direction with a within-industry residual.
sources.limitations: Abstract only (full text not opened: EFMA draft unreachable, SSRN not fetched); monthly horizon, sample ends about 2010.

sources.claim: Avellaneda and Lee (Quantitative Finance 2010, working-paper version): on US stocks above 1 bn market cap, 60-day residual window, ETF or PCA factors, entry at 1.25 sd and exit at 0.5 sd, 5 bp per trade slippage; PCA strategies have an average annual Sharpe of 1.44 over 1997-2007 and only 0.9 in 2003-2007; ETF strategies about 1.1; volume-adjusted (trading-time) signals reach 1.51 in 2003-2007.
sources.core_claim: Avellaneda and Lee (Quantitative Finance 2010, working-paper version): on US stocks above 1 bn market cap, 60-day residual window, ETF or PCA factors, entry at 1.25 sd and exit at 0.5 sd, 5 bp per trade slippage; PCA strategies have an average annual Sharpe of 1.44 over 1997-2007 and only 0.9 in 2003-2007; ETF strategies about 1.1; volume-adjusted (trading-time) signals reach 1.51 in 2003-2007.
sources.applicability: Fixes the PCA residual recipe and gives the pre-/post-2003 decline as the prior.
sources.independent_replication: Khandani and Lo 2007 contrarian strategies reproduced in the same paper; no 2024+ replication found.
sources.limitations: Authors' backtest ending 2007, flat 5 bp, no borrow cost.
sources.market_and_period: US stocks above 1 bn market cap, 1996/2002-2007, daily

sources.claim: Nagel (NBER w17653, Review of Financial Studies 2012): short-term reversal returns proxy the return to liquidity provision; the expected return is strongly time-varying and highly predictable with the VIX index; conditional Sharpe ratios rise with VIX in turmoil such as 2007-09.
sources.core_claim: Nagel (NBER w17653, Review of Financial Studies 2012): short-term reversal returns proxy the return to liquidity provision; the expected return is strongly time-varying and highly predictable with the VIX index; conditional Sharpe ratios rise with VIX in turmoil such as 2007-09.
sources.independent_replication: Hameed-Kang-Viswanathan 2010 find reversal returns after market declines (cited in the paper).
sources.limitations: Sample ends 2009; no cost-net trading result.
sources.market_and_period: US stocks 1926-2009, daily and monthly reversal portfolios

sources.claim: Da, Liu and Schaumburg (Management Science 60(3), 2014): the part of a past return not explained by fundamental (cash-flow) news reverses; the monthly Sharpe of the residual-based reversal is 0.52 versus 0.14 for the standard one; the effect still exists among large stocks in more recent years once the industry momentum effect is controlled for.
sources.core_claim: Da, Liu and Schaumburg (Management Science 60(3), 2014): the part of a past return not explained by fundamental (cash-flow) news reverses; the monthly Sharpe of the residual-based reversal is 0.52 versus 0.14 for the standard one; the effect still exists among large stocks in more recent years once the industry momentum effect is controlled for.
sources.applicability: Supports the industry/no-news residual and the large-stock prior.
sources.independent_replication: Blitz et al. 2013 reach the same direction with a Fama-French residual.
sources.limitations: Monthly, analyst-revision proxy for news, no daily costs.

sources.core_claim: Open-source test (CRSP daily 2000-2024, survivorship-free, one-day hold, 7 bp flat cost): leave-one-out sector-residual reversal has in-sample 2000-2018 gross Sharpe 0.90 and net 0.34, and out-of-sample 2019-2024 gross 0.23 and net -0.15 (breakeven 4.2 bp); the alpha sits in short positions and low-priced names; the PCA(15) variant had no gross edge 2019-2024 (-0.07).
